newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israelis wound three Palestinians in Hebron.
newsitem.headline: Israelis wound three Palestinians in Hebron.

text.p: Israeli soldiers wounded three Palestinians on Thursday during a sixth day of clashes in the West Bank town of Hebron, and a PLO official sounded a warning of dangers ahead if the deadlock in peacemaking could not be broken.
Dozens of Palestinian youths taunted and threw stones at Israeli soldiers across the line that divides Hebron into PLO and Israeli-controlled sections, witnesses said.
At one point, youths threw 10 petrol bombs at soldiers guarding some 400 Jewish settlers who live or study in fortified enclaves in the heart of the town of 100,000 Palestinians. No one was hurt.
Israeli troops, who had fanned out across roofs and balconies and in the town's narrow alleyways since the morning, fired rubber bullets at demonstrators, wounding three.
Palestinian police stayed away from the area of the clashes.

The incidents underscored tensions over a three-month impasse in Israeli-Palestine Liberation Organisation (PLO) peace moves and Israel's expansion of Jewish settlement in the Gaza Strip and the West Bank, including Arab East Jerusalem.

An Egyptian mediation drive to revive substantive talks between Israel and the Palestinians that were broken off when the Jewish state began work on a new settlement in Arab East Jerusalem has so far failed to bear fruit.

Marwan Kanafani, a spokesman for Palestinian President Yasser Arafat, said that failure of Egyptian efforts to revive peace talks would lift "the last barricade against a confrontation between the Israeli and Palestinian sides".
"This is a dangerous thing which we hope will never happen," he told a news conference at the West Bank town of al-Bireh.
In Gaza, Israeli soldiers guarding a Jewish settlement shot and wounded a Palestinian overnight, military sources said.

Israeli military sources said a patrol at the Gush Katif settlement block saw two Arabs near the settlement's fence and called on them to halt. When they did not, it opened fire, wounding one. The two fled to Palestinian Authority territory.
Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu has accused the PLO of orchestrating the unrest. The PLO rejects the charge, saying settlement is at the root of the violence.
Israel demands a PLO crackdown on militants in order to resume talks. The Palestinians want Netanyahu to call a halt to settlement activity which it says pre-empts final peace talks.
